data_quality_notes:
Research ran to completion and logged a RESEARCH COMPLETE block, so nothing here is a truncated report. Nine candidates were captured and all nine are published: six are management instructions on positions already open (GE, UNP, XLE, TLT, SNX, SMMT) and three are new ideas (ISRG, LMT, CMCSA). Position updates are position management, not new risk.

PRICES. Saturday 2026-10-17. Every equity and ETF price in this report is the Friday 2026-10-16 16:00 ET close, fetched from finnhub with session=closed and re-verified at synthesis — a closed market, not stale data. There is no intraday price available and none is implied. Equities are week-ahead prep: entries are for the Monday 2026-10-19 open or later, as each catalyst.action states.

WHAT COULD NOT BE CHECKED, and it is a lot today:
- Options-implied moves: unavailable for every name (yahoo-options HTTP 401). No target in this report was checked against a straddle, including five ideas sitting in front of earnings. This is the biggest hole in today's level-setting.
- Index and volatility levels: ^GSPC, ^NDX, ^DJI, ^RUT, ^VIX, DXY, WTI and gold futures all failed (yahoo HTTP 429, finnhub requires a CFD index subscription, stooq 404s on caret symbols, no alphavantage key). THERE IS NO VIX LEVEL IN THIS REPORT. SPY/QQQ/IWM/TLT/GLD/XLE closes are used as proxies and are labelled as such.
- Event contracts: total loss. market_data.py events returns count 0 for FEDDECISION, CPI, Bitcoin and recession. No implied probability could be quoted, so no event candidate was possible and the two open event positions (KXFEDDECISION-26OCT-H25 YES @28, KXCPIYOY-26SEP-T3.5 NO @18) could not be marked to market.
- Robinhood venue verification: total loss. All three product URLs 404, including the one config/universe.md names. Per the verify-at-runtime rule, no futures or event-contract recommendation was made. Today's list is US-listed equities and ETFs only, where tradeability is not in doubt.
- Crypto levels: no daily history from any source for BTC-USD or BINANCE:BTCUSDT, so no ATR, 20-day or 50-day. Spot prices are quoted; a stop cannot be sited on a proxy, so no crypto candidate. A measured ETH-underperforms-BTC divergence (ETHA -11.1% vs IBIT -5.0% since 10/05) was dropped rather than mis-expressed, because shorting it requires /MET and the venue could not be verified.
- Inflation: macro's cpi_yoy field returns 336.298, the Sep-2026 CPI index level, not a rate. No inflation rate is quoted anywhere in this report.
- Short interest: api.nasdaq.com read-timed out on ISRG and was not retried for the others.
- History depth: history --days 120 returns correct aggregates but only ~20 recent bars, so resistance between the current price and the 120-day high cannot be sited. ISRG and LMT therefore anchor targets to the range high or one ATR below it, stated in their evidence.

WEEKEND SKEW, stated rather than apologised for: 8 of 9 ideas are equities/ETFs, with no futures, no crypto and no event contract on a Saturday — the opposite of what the weekend guidance expects. The cause is not a thin tape; all three weekend-tradeable venues were unverifiable or unpriceable today.

WHY THE LIST IS NINE AND NOT MORE: nine ideas were rejected and logged (VLO and PG for having no honest target at the 120-day high, ABT for having no honest stop, STLD on Friday's reversal bar into its entry, IBM on a 9.1-point drop in bullish share, NFLX on four straight misses at 26.6x, GD on the correlation cap, AAL because the move happened without a fill, the ETH short on venue). The recurring wall is arithmetic: with ATRs near 2% of price and most names ~10% below their 120-day highs, a 2.0 ATR stop plus the 2.0 R:R floor demands a target that lands at or above the prior high. That is the floor working, not a thin day.

RATIOS: the five conviction-4 ideas land at 2.06, 2.11, 2.13, 2.41 and 2.45 against a 2.0 floor, which is the clustering pattern that normally signals targets fitted to clear the bar. Three things argue it is not that here: every target is anchored to a named level (the 120-day high, or one ATR below it) rather than back-solved, every stop sits 2.33-2.71 ATR below entry — comfortably over the floor, so the ratios are not being bought with a tight stop — and three ideas (VLO, PG, STLD) were rejected precisely because the only target that cleared the floor was not a level. TLT sits exactly at 2.00.

TWO IDEAS ARE PUBLISHED WITH NEGATIVE EXPECTANCY ON PURPOSE. SNX (win probability 0.08 against a 0.324 break-even) and SMMT (0.12 against 0.314) are open positions sitting 0.44 and 0.20 of an ATR above their stops. Both are hold-and-do-not-add instructions, not buys, and both carry catalyst.wait. Stating the real probability and letting enforcement demote them to the watchlist is the honest handling; inflating either to survive validation is the failure mode phases 2b-2d exist to catch. Separately, SNX's stop of 242.5 is 1.82 ATR from its 260 entry, under the 2.0 stock floor — a defect in the position as published on 2026-09-19, not something set today. It was not 'fixed' by moving the stop. The same pre-existing defect was found on two open positions not re-pitched here: CEG (stop 1.32 ATR from entry on a 6.15% ATR name) and FCX (1.84 ATR).

XLE's 0.72 win probability is not a claimed 40-point edge. It is arithmetic on a position already 73% of the way to its target: from 68.24 the target is 1.70 ATR away and the stop 5.59 ATR away, so even a driftless walk touches the target first ~77% of the time. The 0.320 baseline is computed from a 63.90 entry this position passed two months ago, and comparing the two overstates the claim by construction.

TRACK RECORD CONTEXT used in sizing: 23 closed trades, 3 hit target (13%), average -5.4%. Conviction 3 is 1/14 and conviction 2 is 0/6, so no conviction-2 idea was published today. The long_term lane is 0/4 with an average of -15.2%, which is why CMCSA is sized at 2% and staged in thirds rather than started at the market.

NOT REVIEWED, recorded as a gap rather than a judgement: seven awaiting-entry names (VST, GLD, OXY, ITB, CVS and the two event contracts) were not reached this run.

RED TEAM (phase 2c). Nine ideas in, six out. Three cut to the watchlist with reasons, three conviction downgrades, two factual corrections.
- Cut SNX: fails the stop-distance check at 1.82 ATR and the expectancy check at -0.75R, both of which the idea's own text identified before it was ranked 8th.
- Cut SMMT: expectancy -0.62R at its own 0.12 win probability, entry 16.9% above the market, stop a fifth of an ATR from the last price.
- Cut TLT: the published 82.0 stop (2.51 ATR, giving exactly 2.0:1) is not the exit the action instructs, which is a weekly close above the 80.73 50-day — 0.99 ATR from entry and 5.06:1. The ratio is an artifact whichever stop is real, and the term-premium view it trades is the same one XLE already carries.
- Downgraded XLE 4 to 3: the 0.72 win probability is sound distance arithmetic on a position 73% to target, but validation pairs it with a reward-to-risk measured from an entry taken on 2026-08-15, so the +1.25R expectancy is an artifact. The remaining trade is 0.30:1 and roughly +0.01R, and the instruction is to exit, not to size up.
- Downgraded GE 4 to 3: the positioning confirmation argues against the idea — 87.5% bullish, the most crowded book screened, with flat revisions — and the leadership claim uses a one-month window where the rest of the report uses three and six.
- Downgraded ISRG 4 to 3: the technical confirmation is the same shelf the key risk expects to break, so a below-market pre-earnings entry is adversely selected, with a 2.38 ATR stop.
- Corrected LMT's 120-day high to 617.00 from 612.75 and ISRG's to 491.15 from 473.86 (ISRG is 13.1% off its high, not 9.95%). Both errors ran conservative for the targets — each sits further below real resistance than claimed — so no target was moved. Both wrong highs had also been used to justify the no-chase instruction in LMT's and ISRG's catalyst.action, and there the corrected number breaks the stated argument: a breakout entry in either name does clear 2.0:1 against the real high. Both instructions are kept and re-argued on the grounds that survive, which in both cases is that a chase entry has no level within 2.0 ATR to stop against.
- Not cut, and checked rather than assumed: UNP's 315.99 target is the genuine 120-day range high on fetched candles, and its 20- and 50-day both reconcile, so the target-feasibility warn at 6.43 ATR is a far real level rather than a number reverse-engineered to clear the floor. UNP and LMT keep conviction 4; they are also the only two ideas whose stops clear 2.5 ATR.
- The five earnings_date warns are a validator artifact, not report errors. Every date and consensus figure was re-fetched and matches exactly: GE 10-19 bmo 2.0576, ISRG 10-20 amc 2.6956, UNP 10-22 bmo 3.5034, LMT 10-22 bmo 7.5112, CMCSA 10-22 bmo 1.0136, plus HAL 10-20, BKR 10-21, VLO 10-22, XOM and SLB 10-23 for XLE.
- Correlation, stated plainly because the cuts made it worse rather than better: with TLT gone there is no short and no non-equity expression left in the report. Five of the six survivors are long cyclicals into one earnings week, UNP, LMT and GE are three industrials measured against the same XLI proxy at 3% each, and XLE is a fourth reflation long, so 12% of the 17% gross sits on one macro path. CMCSA at 2% is the only idea that does not. Sizing was left alone on the three open positions, GE, XLE and UNP, since the instructions already reduce rather than add, but the concentration is real and is not diversification.
- Nothing in the options-implied hole was fixable here: five of the six survivors still report inside their holding period with no straddle to check a target against.

market_context.summary: A tech-led de-rating against a 5.10% long end. Friday 2026-10-16 closed SPY -1.11%, QQQ -2.50% and IWM -1.69%: QQQ fell 2.3x SPY, so this was long-duration growth repricing rather than generic beta. The dominant macro fact is the curve — the 10-year yields 5.10% against an effective fed funds rate of 3.88% with a +0.35 10y-2y spread, so 122bp of the long end is term premium rather than policy pass-through, and the market is pricing supply and inflation risk rather than cuts. Energy was the only thing up and up a lot, XLE +2.52% to a 120-day-high close, which is the one sector this rate regime pays rather than discounts. Crypto was broadly weak with majors down least (BTC -0.46%, ETH -0.48%) and high-beta alts down 2-4x as much, which is risk-off inside crypto rather than rotation. Regional banks are notably not being paid for the steeper curve: FITB, ZION, WAL and WTFC all sit 13-15% below their 120-day highs and only 4-8% above their lows while XLF is just 5.3% off its high, so XLF's strength is coming from money-centre and capital-markets names, not from net interest margin. The week ahead is the heavy part of Q3 season — 1,338 calendar events in 12 days, with META, TSLA, XOM and five energy names reporting into open positions. No VIX level was obtainable today.

catalyst.event: Q3 earnings Thu 2026-10-22 before open ET, consensus EPS 7.5112 on revenue $20.69B
catalyst.action: The entry at 532 is BELOW the market at 552.09 and sits at the top of the unfilled 523.08-531.00 gap left on 2026-10-15. Buy that zone if it is offered, before or after the print. Do not chase 552 and do not buy a breakout above 553.14. Red team corrected the reason: the 120-day high is 617.00, not the 612.75 this instruction was written against, and on the real number a 553 breakout entry with a 2.0 ATR stop would clear 2.0:1 — so the arithmetic originally given for not chasing does not hold. The instruction stands on what does: above 553 there is no base within 20 points to site a stop on, the nearest shelf being 523-531 and then 497-499, so any stop up there is a round number rather than a level; and Bernstein's $564 price target is 2% above a 553 entry, which is the covering analyst saying the stock is at fair value. The gap entry is the whole discipline of this idea - it is where the trade avoids paying the announcement premium, and a breakout entry is a different, worse trade rather than the same one later. If the gap never fills, the trade does not happen.

recommendations.thesis: Lockheed re-rated 9.5% in four sessions, 504.02 on 2026-10-13 to 552.09 on 2026-10-16, closing Friday near its 553.14 high on a day SPY fell 1.11%, and the mechanism is specific rather than sentiment: the company is scaling missile and munitions production, with a roughly $14.7B award placed with Boeing to triple PAC-3 MSE seeker output, a $300M Texas missile-production investment, and a stated plan to add 6,000 US jobs. Analyst bullish share jumped 7.1 points in four months to 46.4%, which is the lowest base of any name screened today, so the sell side is upgrading into the move from a long way behind it. Earnings Thursday is the test.
recommendations.key_risk: The entry is 3.6% below the market and may simply never fill: a four-session re-rating that closes at its high does not often hand back 20 points, and if Thursday's print is good the 523-531 gap stays open. The opposite risk is the one that costs money - the gap fills because the print is bad. Bernstein cut its price target to $564 on funding-delay worries, which is 2.2% above Friday's close, so at least one covering analyst thinks the stock is already at fair value, and defense revenue recognition turns on appropriations timing that a production announcement does not accelerate. Correction from the red team: the 120-day high is 617.00 on fetched candles, not the 612.75 the evidence states. The error runs the safe way — 602 is 1.4 ATR below the real high rather than 1.0 — so the target stands, but the number it was derived from was wrong.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that announcements of future capacity are not earnings: a seeker-production award placed with a supplier and a plan to hire 6,000 people are cash out before they are cash in, and LMT is -6.77% over six months against SPY +7.48%, a 14.25-point deficit, so this is a bounce in a de-rated name with a funding-delay overhang Bernstein has already written down to $564. The answer is in the three-month measurement rather than the six: LMT is +8.35% over three months against SPY +2.85% and XLI -5.82%, so +5.50 and +14.17 points of outperformance, it is above both its 20-day at 516.62 and its 50-day at 543.16, and the earnings record supports the print rather than the narrative - +10.51% (Jun-26), +28.99% (Dec-25), +8.18% (Sep-25) against one miss of -5.20% (Mar-26). The entry is set in the gap precisely so the idea is not paying the announcement premium.

catalyst.action: DO NOT BUY BEFORE THE PRINT. Price is 426.70 and the entry is 413, which is deliberately below the market. If the Tuesday reaction takes it into the 411-416 shelf and it holds the 20-day at 411.16, buy there in one clip. If it instead gaps above 435, the pullback entry is void for this week - do not chase it higher. Red team corrected the reason: the 120-day high is 491.15, not the 473.86 this instruction cited, and from 435 a 2.0 ATR stop against a target below the real high does clear 2.0:1, so headroom is not the objection. The objection is the stop: above 435 the 411-416 shelf and the 391 double bottom are the only real levels, both more than 2.0 ATR away, so a chase entry has nothing to stop against except the price it paid. Buying the gap up is also paying the reaction to a print this idea is positioned ahead of, which is the opposite of the setup.

recommendations.thesis: Intuitive has beaten consensus four quarters running by 9.8%, 16.8%, 9.9% and 18.7% - an average of 13.8% - and the stock has turned up on it, running 391.95 on 2026-10-02 to a 434.89 high on 2026-10-16 while holding above both its 20-day at 411.16 and its 50-day at 391.67. It is still 13.1% below its 120-day high of 491.15 after a severe first-half de-rating (red-team corrected from the 9.95% off 473.86 stated at synthesis), so the recovery is reclaiming ground rather than making new ground, and the entry is placed at the 411-416 shelf the last breakout left behind rather than at Friday's 426.70.
recommendations.key_risk: The entry fills on a disappointing reaction, which is the failure mode this report has already paid for: a pullback entry below the market is reached first by the ideas that are going wrong. Specifically, a procedure-volume or da Vinci 5 placement miss would take ISRG through 411 without pausing, and a 2.56% ATR means the 413 entry and the 387 stop are only 2.4 ATR apart - one bad gap covers most of that. Short interest could not be checked: the nasdaq source read-timed out. Red team, on conviction: the score comes down to 3 because the three listed confirmations are not three. The technical_level confirmation is the 411-416 shelf, and the key risk above is that a procedure-volume or da Vinci 5 miss goes through 411 without pausing — so the level cannot be independent support for an entry that only fills if that is what happens. A below-market entry ahead of a print is adversely selected: the fills come from the reactions that went wrong. With the stop at 2.38 ATR, under the 2.5 level where this report's stop-outs have clustered, that leaves a dated catalyst and improving revisions, which is a 3.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that this is a dead-cat bounce dressed as leadership: ISRG is -9.06% over six months against SPY +7.48% and XLV +18.76%, a 27.8-point deficit to its own sector, so the name is broken and the last three months are mean reversion that stops when it reaches supply. Answered with the measured three-month turn rather than assertion: ISRG is +20.82% over three months against SPY +2.85% and XLV +10.96%, so +17.97 and +9.86 points of outperformance, and it is above both moving averages with revisions improving to 72.5% bullish and 13 strong buys. A bounce that has lasted three months, led its sector throughout, and is backed by four consecutive double-digit earnings beats is a re-rating on fundamentals. Insider buying does not support it either way - zero open-market purchases in six months against 35 routine sales worth $8.08M at a company of this size, which is comp-related flow rather than a signal.

recommendations.thesis: Comcast has reported 1.04, 0.79, 0.84 and 1.12 over its last four quarters, so trailing EPS is 3.79 against a 21.90 price - 5.78x earnings on a $77.7B market cap, with three beats in those four quarters and analyst revisions improving. The entry is deliberately set below the 120-day low because the one thing wrong with the idea is that nothing has stopped falling yet.
recommendations.key_risk: The core business is in structural decline and a low multiple on a shrinking earnings base is not cheap, it is correctly priced - the trap in every cable value thesis. Management is not buying either: zero open-market insider purchases in six months, and zero insider sales too, so there is no insider signal in either direction at a stock trading at 5.8x. This lane is also the report's worst: long_term is 0 for 4 on hitting target with an average of -15.2%, which argues for a higher bar rather than a bigger position, hence 2% and a staged entry. INVALIDATION, which replaces a stop: trailing four-quarter EPS falling below 3.20, or EPS missing consensus in two consecutive quarters. Either would mean the earnings base is eroding faster than the multiple can recover, and the thesis is then wrong regardless of price.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is momentum, and it is unanimous: CMCSA lags SPY on every window measured, -4.41% over one month, -7.91% over three and -26.09% over six against SPY +0.09%, +2.85% and +7.48%, and it lags its own sector proxy XLC by 2.60, 7.48 and 18.72 points over the same windows. Buying that is catching something falling relative to everything around it. This is not answered away, it is answered structurally: the entry is placed under 20.50, below the 120-day low, so the idea only ever starts if the decline first reaches a level, and it is staged in thirds down to 19.00 rather than committed at once. What the valuation work does answer is whether the fall has gone far enough to matter - at 5.78x trailing against a 4.5x bear case the downside is 22% while the 7.5x re-rating is 30% up from the entry, and the business beat consensus in three of the last four quarters while the multiple was compressing, which is the gap between the earnings and the price that the trade is buying. Red team adds the gap neither side closes: nothing in this thesis says why the multiple re-rates. 7.5x and the 4.5x bear case are both asserted, and the key risk above concedes the cable trap — that a low multiple on a shrinking earnings base is correct pricing rather than cheapness — which is an argument the valuation work does not answer. What survives scrutiny is narrower than the thesis claims: the one hard anchor on the 28.40 target is that 28.31 is a price the market actually paid inside the last 120 days, so this is a round-trip-to-a-traded-level target that happens to coincide with 7.5x, not a multiple the evidence establishes. Held at conviction 3 and 2% on that basis, with the staged entry below the 120-day low and the EPS invalidation doing the work a stop would.
